questions.stem: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror so that it makes an angle of 30° with the surface of the mirror. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: Angles are measured from the normal. The angle with the surface is 30°, so the angle of incidence is 90° − 30° = 60°, and the angle of reflection is also 60°.

questions.stem: An object is placed beyond the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image formed is:
options: Virtual, erect and behind the mirror
Real, inverted and diminished, between F and C
Real, inverted and the same size, at C
questions.explanation: For an object beyond C, the reflected rays actually meet between F and C, forming a real, inverted, smaller image that can be caught on a screen.

questions.stem: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. Using the sign convention, the image distance v is:
questions.explanation: u = −30 cm, f = −20 cm. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/20 + 1/30 = −1/60, so v = −60 cm: a real image 60 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.stem: Light travels from air into glass of refractive index 1.5. If the speed of light in air is 3 × 10⁸ m/s, its speed in the glass is:
questions.explanation: n = c/v, so v = c/n = 3 × 10⁸ / 1.5 = 2 × 10⁸ m/s. Light slows down in a denser medium.

questions.stem: Lens A is a convex lens of focal length 10 cm and lens B is a convex lens of focal length 40 cm. Which lens is more powerful and what is its power?
questions.explanation: P = 1/f with f in metres. Lens A: 1/0.10 = +10 D. Lens B: 1/0.40 = +2.5 D. A shorter focal length means a more powerful lens.

questions.stem: A student can see nearby objects clearly but the blackboard looks blurred. Which lens will correct this defect?
options: A convex lens of suitable power
A concave lens of suitable power
questions.explanation: This is myopia: the image forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays slightly so that the image falls on the retina.

questions.stem: Why does the clear sky appear blue?
options: The sea reflects its blue colour onto the sky
Air molecules scatter blue light much more than red light
Red light is scattered the most, leaving blue behind
The atmosphere absorbs all colours except blue
questions.explanation: Shorter wavelengths (blue) are scattered far more strongly by air molecules than longer wavelengths (red), so scattered blue light reaches our eyes from every part of the sky.

questions.stem: In a simple circuit with a battery and one bulb, an ammeter placed before the bulb reads 0.5 A. An identical ammeter placed after the bulb will read:
options: Less than 0.5 A, because the bulb uses up some current
0 A, because the bulb uses up all the current
questions.explanation: Current is the flow of charge and charge is conserved; it is not used up. The bulb converts electrical energy to light and heat, but the same current flows through every part of a series circuit.

questions.stem: A 6 V battery is connected across a 12 Ω resistor and 0.5 A flows. The resistor is replaced by a 6 Ω resistor. The current now is:
options: 0.5 A, because the battery always gives the same current
questions.explanation: The battery fixes the voltage (6 V), not the current. I = V/R = 6/6 = 1 A. Halving the resistance doubles the current.

questions.stem: A copper wire has a resistance of 4 Ω. Another copper wire of the same cross-section area but twice the length will have a resistance of:
options: 4 Ω, because the material is the same
questions.explanation: R = ρl/A. With ρ and A unchanged, resistance is proportional to length, so doubling the length doubles the resistance to 8 Ω.

questions.stem: Two 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. A third 6 Ω resistor is then added in parallel. The equivalent resistance changes from:
questions.explanation: Two in parallel: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3, so R = 3 Ω. Three in parallel: 1/R = 3/6 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω. Every extra parallel branch lowers the total resistance.

questions.stem: A 100 W bulb and a 40 W bulb, both rated 220 V, are connected in series across a 220 V supply. Which statement is correct?
options: The 100 W bulb glows brighter because it has the higher rating
The 40 W bulb glows brighter because it has the higher resistance and the same current flows through both
Both glow equally because the same current flows through both
Neither glows because the voltage is shared
questions.explanation: R = V²/P, so the 40 W bulb has the larger resistance. In series the current is the same, and P = I²R, so the larger resistance dissipates more power and glows brighter.

questions.stem: Which of these statements about magnetic field lines is correct?
options: Two field lines can cross where the field is strong
Outside a magnet, field lines go from the south pole to the north pole
No two field lines ever intersect each other
Field lines are closer together where the field is weaker
questions.explanation: If two lines crossed, the field would have two directions at that point, which is impossible. Outside a magnet lines go from N to S, and they are closer where the field is stronger.

questions.stem: A straight conductor carrying current is placed in a uniform magnetic field, with the current perpendicular to the field. The force on the conductor acts:
options: Along the direction of the magnetic field
Perpendicular to both the current and the magnetic field
Opposite to the direction of the magnetic field
Along the direction of the current
questions.explanation: By Fleming's left-hand rule, force, field and current are mutually perpendicular: F = BIL sin θ, directed perpendicular to both B and I.
